item.title: Front-end developer (UI) for Corro — an accessibility-first board & card game platform
item.dc:creator: Corro
item.description: Corro is an accessibility-first engine for online board and card games — built so that everyone plays the same game together, whatever their abilities. The name evokes a circle of people holding hands as equals, with no head of the table. Accessibility is the foundation of the codebase, not an afterthought. You can try it live at https://allwelcome.games. I’m the founder, and I’m blind. The engine already treats accessibility as a first-class concern — ARIA live regions for game announcements, full keyboard navigation and focus management, native dialog modals with focus trapping, semantic HTML and server-authoritative announcements. What the front-end needs now is polish: a UI that is as visually refined and pleasant as it is accessible.
item.content:encoded:
Organization: Corro

Status: searching

Compensation: gratis

Role: Front-end development, UI implementation

Corro is an accessibility-first engine for online board and card games — built so that everyone plays the same game together, whatever their abilities. The name evokes a circle of people holding hands as equals, with no head of the table. Accessibility is the foundation of the codebase, not an afterthought. You can try it live at https://allwelcome.games.

I’m the founder, and I’m blind. The engine already treats accessibility as a first-class concern — ARIA live regions for game announcements, full keyboard navigation and focus management, native dialog modals with focus trapping, semantic HTML and server-authoritative announcements. What the front-end needs now is polish: a UI that is as visually refined and pleasant as it is accessible.

What we’re looking for

A front-end developer to improve and beautify Corro’s interface — refining layout, responsiveness and visual detail across the lobby and in-game screens — without breaking the accessibility that is the whole point of the project. You’d work closely with our illustrator/designer to bring the visual layer to life in the browser.

Tech stack

  • Vanilla TypeScript (no bundler), vanilla CSS
  • i18next for localization (English & Spanish today)
  • Backend is .NET 10 / ASP.NET Core / SignalR — but this role is front-end focused

What you’d help with

  • Refining and beautifying the lobby and in-game UI (CSS, layout, responsive/mobile)
  • Integrating new artwork and icons into the interface
  • Keeping everything keyboard-navigable and screen-reader friendly as the UI evolves
  • Small, well-scoped improvements to focus management, live regions and semantic markup

A good fit if you

  • Are comfortable with modern vanilla TypeScript and CSS (no framework required)
  • Take accessibility seriously — or want to get genuinely good at it
  • Enjoy careful, detail-oriented UI work
  • Are happy contributing to an AGPL-3.0 open-source project

This is a volunteer role. If you want your front-end skills to help build a more inclusive place to play, get in touch.

How to Apply:

  • juanjo@jmontiel.es
  • https://github.com/kastwey/corro

item.title: Illustrator & graphic designer for Corro — an accessibility-first board & card game platform
item.dc:creator: Corro
item.description: Corro is an accessibility-first engine for online board and card games — designed so that everyone plays the same game together, whatever their abilities. The name comes from the image of a circle of people holding hands as equals, with no head of the table. Accessibility isn’t a feature we bolt on; it’s the foundation of the architecture. You can try the live platform at https://allwelcome.games. I’m the founder, and I’m blind. I’ve built the engine so that a blind player and a sighted player can share the exact same match — same board, same cards, same turns. item.content:encoded:
Organization: Corro

Status: searching

Compensation: gratis

Role: Illustration, game art, graphic design

Corro is an accessibility-first engine for online board and card games — designed so that everyone plays the same game together, whatever their abilities. The name comes from the image of a circle of people holding hands as equals, with no head of the table. Accessibility isn’t a feature we bolt on; it’s the foundation of the architecture. You can try the live platform at https://allwelcome.games.

I’m the founder, and I’m blind. I’ve built the engine so that a blind player and a sighted player can share the exact same match — same board, same cards, same turns. What I can’t do myself is make that shared world beautiful to look at. That’s where you come in.

What we’re looking for

An illustrator / graphic designer to give Corro’s games a warm, cohesive visual identity: illustrating cards, tiles, boards, pieces and other in-game elements, and helping shape a consistent art style across the platform. Your work would be the visual layer of a game that blind and sighted people can finally enjoy side by side.

What you’d help with

  • Illustrations for cards, tiles, boards, tokens and game pieces
  • A coherent visual style and small art guidelines others can follow
  • Icons and visual elements for the game interface
  • Delivering artwork in open, reusable formats (SVG preferred where possible) so it can ship inside Corro’s .corro game packages

A good fit if you

  • Love game art and illustration and want your work to have real social impact
  • Care about (or are curious about) inclusive and accessible design
  • Are happy collaborating in the open on an AGPL-3.0 project
  • Bonus: any experience with high-contrast, colour-blind-friendly or otherwise accessible visual design

This is a volunteer role on an open-source project. If sharing play — rather than gatekeeping it — is something you believe in, I’d love to build this with you.

How to Apply:

  • juanjo@jmontiel.es
  • https://github.com/kastwey/corro

item.title: UX support/input working with disabled people to help design the next version of the fastest text entry system

item.title: UX (re)design
item.dc:creator: InvenTree
item.description: InvenTree is an open-source PLM (parts libary managment) with a backend API server, a frontend based on Bootstrap/jquery /JS-based frontend and several apps. We are rewriting the frontend based on React and want to take this opportunity to create a more user-friendly, intuitive and accessible experience for everyone. Major pain points are: Navigation between pages Information-dense but readable tables Introducing users to functions, communicating restrictions and possible actions The credentials for the demo can be found here: https://inventree.org/demo, the current state of the new UI is accessible here
item.content:encoded:
Organization: InvenTree

Status: closed

Compensation: gratis

Role: Web design, Interaction design, Accessibility testing

InvenTree is an open-source PLM (parts libary managment) with a backend API server, a frontend based on Bootstrap/jquery /JS-based frontend and several apps. We are rewriting the frontend based on React and want to take this opportunity to create a more user-friendly, intuitive and accessible experience for everyone.

Major pain points are:

  • Navigation between pages
  • Information-dense but readable tables
  • Introducing users to functions, communicating restrictions and possible actions

The credentials for the demo can be found here: https://inventree.org/demo, the current state of the new UI is accessible here

A designer already did some groundwork and we have some great mockups (figma) available, he had to reallocate his free time. We have coders on the team so getting designs/behaviours built once they are conceptualised should not be a problem - you do not need to know how to code.

How to Apply:

  • Matthias (memeber of core team) <code@mjmair.com>
  • https://docs.inventree.org/en/latest/develop/contributing/

item.title: Graphic designer for OpenScore
item.dc:creator: OpenScore
item.description: OpenScore is a collaboration between MuseScore, IMSLP, and various other partners across the music and tech industries. The aim is to unite MuseScore’s millions of users in a crowdsource effort digitise and liberate the works of Mozart, Beethoven and other famous classical composers. Digital sheet music provides convenient sharing, adaptation and playback across a range of devices, including computers, phones and tablets. The scores will be made available in a variety of formats, including PDF, MIDI and MusicXML, as well as accessible formats like Braille and Modified Stave Notation for blind and partially sighted musicians. The scores will be released under a Creative Commons license to remove all copyright restrictions. This will be of huge benefit to orchestras, choirs and individuals looking for materials from which to practise music. It will also facilitate a number of uses in research, academia, and education, and help to inspire composers and arrangers in producing new content.
item.content:encoded:
Organization: OpenScore

Status: filled

Compensation: paid

OpenScore is a collaboration between MuseScore, IMSLP, and various other partners across the music and tech industries. The aim is to unite MuseScore’s millions of users in a crowdsource effort digitise and liberate the works of Mozart, Beethoven and other famous classical composers.

Digital sheet music provides convenient sharing, adaptation and playback across a range of devices, including computers, phones and tablets. The scores will be made available in a variety of formats, including PDF, MIDI and MusicXML, as well as accessible formats like Braille and Modified Stave Notation for blind and partially sighted musicians. The scores will be released under a Creative Commons license to remove all copyright restrictions. This will be of huge benefit to orchestras, choirs and individuals looking for materials from which to practise music. It will also facilitate a number of uses in research, academia, and education, and help to inspire composers and arrangers in producing new content.

OpenScore will be running a Kickstarter campaign to fund the transcription effort, and we will be seeking to raise its profile at a number of upcoming music and tech conferences. We are looking for a designer who is familiar with open source and Creative Commons, and who can help us to illustrate these concepts in a way the general public can understand.

How to Apply:

Email openscore@musescore.com with links to CV and portfolio.
